title: Cardinal Campeggio's conclave articles for Francis I, c. 1534 (BnF fr. 3081 ff. 41-42, DECODE R2322; catalogued as French marshals to the King, 1520)

documents.date: c. October 1534 (from the cardinals named; DECODE gives 1 Jan 1520)
documents.route: Cardinal Lorenzo Campeggio (articles sworn to the cardinals Bourbon, Lorraine, Tournon) to Francis I; endorsed as from the marshals

plaintext.source: George Lasry's key and decipherment of f. 41r (24 May 2022), on Tomokiyo's cryptiana; f. 41v had no published reading

transcription.source: f. 41v (DECODE image P2) read sign by sign into plaintext letters with Lasry's key; f. 41r not transcribed
transcription.notes: The measured file holds the deciphered letters of f. 41v (37 lines), not sign codes; bracketed code signs such as [CON] add a few letters.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution with invented graphic signs, 20 letters with 1-4 signs each plus code signs for CON and ET, no word division.
system.notes: Same key reads BnF Dupuy 265 f. 132 (Mâcon to the King, 1535) per Lasry. On f. 41v: Lasry's third H sign = Y, 'Rg' = P, looped 4 = R, unknown ʃ = S (C); one unknown cluster probably a code for the Emperor (M).

prior_solution.where: Lasry's key table and f. 41r overlays on cryptiana (francis.htm, GL.htm), 2022

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code with Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE R2322's four images with the shared cookie: f. 41r and f. 41v cipher, f. 42r blank, f. 42v endorsement.
Tomokiyo's francis.htm (as the catalogue suggested): 'George Lasry solved it in 2022'; downloaded his key table and three f. 41r overlays from GL.htm. They cover f. 41r only.
Two subagents read f. 41v (lines 1-19, 20-37) sign by sign with Lasry's table, using his f. 41r overlays as a training sheet.
f. 41v reads with about 90-95% of letters secure after re-valuing four signs (Y, P, R, S); four sign groups and one code sign open; the page breaks off mid-sentence.

Dated from content: Campeggio's articles sworn to Bourbon, Lorraine and Tournon (cardinal 1530; Campeggio d. 1539) and the papal-candidate clause fit the October 1534 conclave, not 1520. Not checked against a conclave history.
Second pass at 3-4x zoom on the 13 doubtful places: 9 settled (l. 8 desquels en avoit, l. 31 vers les detenteurs, bold ʃ = S confirmed), 4 open.
Third pass on the two words left without sense: l. 12 OCVPEES 'oc[c]upees'; l. 15 a sign misread as E is M row 2 (as in 'en ma-'), giving 'des armes'. Coverage counted: 1,339/1,341 tokens.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): f. 41v letter stream and line-by-line sign transcriptions linked, running decryption copied from NOTES.md to texts/f41v_decryption.md, key adjustments copied to texts/key.md; f. 41r points to Lasry's overlays on cryptiana GL.htm (his f. 41r text is not in the repository).

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): texts/f41v_decryption.md reads (A); f. 41r points only to Lasry's overlay images, with no text in the repository. f. 41r relabelled decoded, not read (excerpt only); class read -> read in part; fraction_read 0.998 -> about 0.5 (estimated).

Every file on DECODE R2322 opened again (P1 f. 41r, P2 f. 41v, P3 f. 42r blank, P4 f. 42v endorsement; no DOC_* text, no other attachment): no contemporary decipherment. George Lasry's f. 41r decipherment transcribed letter by letter from his three overlay crops (cryptiana GL.htm; the crops overlap by one line and cover 4 heading + 31 body lines) into texts/f41r_lasry_overlay.txt (1,165 letters).

Overlay letters checked against the figures on P1 at native resolution at seven places (texts/f41r_corrections.tsv): l. 7 end is the Rg sign (P, the f. 41v value in every occurrence), 'par armes' for the overlay's DAR; l. 1 end is the Rc sign (D) where the sense needs 'par', kept [?par]; l. 2 Rc = D in 'de doumage'; l. 7 'l'ung a voulu'; l. 22 the overlay's S is the C sign, 'pacificque'; l. 28 the 'ʃκ' pair is two signs, 'si esplore' (éploré); l. 13-14 a repeated phrase. No key value changed.

Reading written from the overlay letters (texts/f41r_reading.md, f41r_en.md, log f41r_reread_log.md); aligned word by word with the overlay, no word supplied, one hole [?par]. b17_score.py (fr) on the body: 0.429 (9/21), explicit holes 1.00 (21/21); before: no text. f. 41r set read, grade B; class read in part -> read; fraction_read 0.5 (estimated) -> 0.999 (measured).

outcome.method_basis: Lasry's 2022 key for BnF fr. 3081 f. 41 (cryptiana GL.htm, francis.htm) read f. 41r before; the project read f. 41v, which had no published reading, with the same key.
outcome.notes: f. 41r read by Lasry 2022; f. 41v read here. fraction_read counted on f41v_letters.txt: 2 of 1,341 tokens without a value (l. 19 sign, l. 30 code). Catalogue entry 195 removed. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: f. 41r decoded, not read here (Lasry's reading exists only as overlay images); class read -> read in part.

gaps.detail: the sign is the Rc look-alike (D) where the sense needs P; one letter

texts.label: f. 41r (George Lasry, 24 May 2022)
texts.summary: The heading and preamble of the articles: 'Articles iures par monsieur le cardinal Campege es mains de messeigneurs les cardinaulx de Bourgon, Loraine et Tornon'. Campeggio sets out the harm the wars of the Christian princes have done to Christendom and the Holy See, his own efforts for a stable peace so that Christendom could turn against the Turk and the heresies, all of which needs the counsel and power of the Most Christian King (the sentence runs on to f. 41v).

reading_review.note: Read 23 Oct 2026 (b30): George Lasry's decipherment (24 May 2022), transcribed for the first time from his three overlay crops (cryptiana GL.htm), which together cover the four heading lines and all 31 body lines; figures checked on the native DECODE image at seven places (l. 7 overlay D = the Rg sign P, 'par armes'; l. 22 'pacificque' and l. 28 'si esplore' resolved on the signs; l. 1 [?par] where the figures give the look-alike D, 1 letter on a look-alike alternate). No word supplied. Body 0.429 clean sentences (9/21), explicit holes 1.00 (21/21); every unclean sentence fails on 1534 spellings and names only; the sentences hold.

texts.label: f. 41v
texts.summary: Francis I refuses to join a crusade against the Turk until Milan, Asti and Genoa are restored to him; Cardinal Campeggio swears that, if elected pope, he will press the Emperor and the holders of Milan to return them. Tournon became a cardinal in 1530 and Campeggio died in 1539, so these are articles for the conclave of October 1534; the page breaks off mid-sentence.

outcome.fraction_read_source: 23 Oct 2026 (b30): both pages read. f. 41r: 1,165 letters (texts/f41r_lasry_overlay.txt, Lasry's decipherment transcribed, figures checked at seven places); f. 41v: 1,339 of 1,341 letter tokens given a value (f41v_letters.txt). (1,165 + 1,339) / (1,165 + 1,341) = 0.999. The articles after f. 41v are not in the volume (needs-physical-access) and are not counted.
